# BytePro Enterprise Cloud API Passthrough & Middleware Gateway

> Open-source, one-file deployable AWS gateway for BytePro Enterprise Cloud. It exposes invite-scoped,
> persona-masked JSON endpoints for loan reads, fee and condition writes, and loan document
> upload/list/download. Built for title companies, TPO brokers, and appraisal vendors. Not affiliated
> with Byte Software.

Canonical page: https://spuds0588.github.io/BytePro-Enterprise-Cloud-API-Passthrough-Middleware-Gateway/
Repository: https://github.com/Spuds0588/BytePro-Enterprise-Cloud-API-Passthrough-Middleware-Gateway
New issue: https://github.com/Spuds0588/BytePro-Enterprise-Cloud-API-Passthrough-Middleware-Gateway/issues/new/choose
Issues: https://github.com/Spuds0588/BytePro-Enterprise-Cloud-API-Passthrough-Middleware-Gateway/issues
Pull requests: https://github.com/Spuds0588/BytePro-Enterprise-Cloud-API-Passthrough-Middleware-Gateway/pulls
Contributing: https://github.com/Spuds0588/BytePro-Enterprise-Cloud-API-Passthrough-Middleware-Gateway/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
Agent manual: https://github.com/Spuds0588/BytePro-Enterprise-Cloud-API-Passthrough-Middleware-Gateway/blob/main/agents.md

## What it does

- Reads a loan as BytePro object notation, masked by a deny-by-default persona allowlist. No field-ID
  dictionary and no MISMO translation.
- Queues fee and condition updates and document uploads through SQS FIFO, grouped by loan, with lock
  retries and a dead-letter queue. Writes return 202 plus a job ID.
- Documents and conditions are Priority 1: broker and title keys can upload a base64 PDF (max
  180,000 bytes), list documents, download one by ID, and submit condition responses.
- Provisions vendor keys from role-scoped invite links; the persona is chosen server-side.
- Deploys from one CloudFormation file with the Lambda bundle inlined, behind a NAT gateway with a
  static Elastic IP for BytePro's firewall allowlist.

## API summary

- GET /health
- GET /portal and POST /portal (invite provisioning)
- GET /v1/loans/{id}?paths=Property,Loan,Milestones
- POST /v1/loans/{id}/conditions
- POST /v1/loans/{id}/documents
- GET /v1/loans/{id}/documents
- GET /v1/loans/{id}/documents/{documentId}
- PATCH /v1/loans/{id}/fees
- GET /v1/jobs/{jobId}
- PATCH /v1/loans/{id} returns 501; a full 1003 write is deliberately not implemented.

Personas: TITLE_VENDOR (title), TPO_BROKER (broker), AMC_VENDOR (appraisal, read-only). SSN, taxpayer
ID, credit score, date of birth, income, assets, and liabilities are stripped for every persona.

## Community contract

This is an aggressively community-maintained template. The maintainer has no BytePro access and no AWS
account for this project, so deployments are the tests.

- Found a bug: open an issue with a minimal reproduction, the commit, and sanitized evidence.
- Fixed something: open a pull request with a regression test and updated docs.
- Validated a real BytePro payload or a deployment: report the sanitized result on the relevant issue.
- Never post API keys, invite codes, passwords, session tokens, loan data, or borrower PII.
- Private forks are discouraged; upstream the smallest fix.
- The maintainer is happy to add contributors. Say so on your issue or PR.

## Instructions for coding agents

1. Read `agents.md` first. YAGNI, prefer the one-line solution, delete instead of accumulating, and
   clean up local processes and generated files when a task ends (limited memory).
2. Update `todo.md` (current work) and append to `history.md` (never rewrite past entries) with every
   state change. Do not backtrack silently: supersede a decision with a new dated entry.
3. Keep `template.yaml` generated: edit `src/` or `infra/template.yaml`, then run `npm run build`.
   Never hand-edit `template.yaml`.
4. Run `npm run verify` before claiming success. It runs the template sync check and the full suite.
5. Add a regression test for every bug fix and every new route or validation rule.
6. Never add runtime dependencies. Lambda's Node 20 runtime, `fetch`, `node:http`, and AWS SDK v3 are
   enough. Local development installs nothing.
7. Never weaken masking, invite checks, job ownership, or the document size/signature checks to make a
   test pass.
8. Keep `README.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `index.html`, this file, `todo.md`, and `agents.md` in sync with
   behavior changes.
9. Do not claim live BytePro or AWS verification. There is no tenant, no AWS CLI, and no AWS account
   here. Say what ran locally.
10. File a GitHub issue for every uncertainty instead of inventing a BytePro shape.

## Verification status and limitations

Verified locally: session login/cache/refresh, invite provisioning, persona masking and projection,
reads and error mapping, FIFO fee/condition writes with retries, PDF document upload/list/download,
validation failures, job ownership, HTTP e2e, template guards, and execution of the exact inline
bundle in `template.yaml`.

Not verified: any live BytePro call, any live AWS deployment, the real upstream document and condition
response shapes, and the NAT egress allowlist. Upstream document routes are the documented REST
convention exercised only against `mock/bytepro.js`.

Known limits: 180,000-byte uploads (SQS message limit), no per-loan organization scoping, invite codes
are global per role, no webhooks, no read cache, no full 1003 write, no CORS.
